Title: Voluntary redundancy programme at the Polish Mining Group
Title (national language): Program dobrowolnych odejść w Polskiej Grupie Górniczej
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Subcategory: Active labour market policies (enhancing employability, training, subsidised job creation, etc.)
Background information: The Polish Mining Group (Polska Grupa Górnicza) has announced plans to make more than 400 people redundant, mostly underground workers. This is due to the company's difficult financial situation.Moreover, the Polish Mining Group is working on a voluntary departure programme. The programme is aimed at people who voluntarily decide to terminate their employment contract. The departure will take place under special conditions.
Content of measure: Redundant employees of Polish Mining Group, who have reached retirement age, received severance payments in cash in the amount resulting from the regulations on group redundancies, severance pay, compensation for reduced notice periods, where applicable, and cash compensation for unused leave.Moreover, in December 2024, employees of the Polish Mining Group were provided with a questionnaire on the voluntary redundancy programme, allowing them to select their preferred options. An additional question has been prepared for employees at the Bielszowice mine regarding the option to be transferred to another PGG division in the event that employment at the Ruda mine is no longer possible.
Use of measure: A total of 435 workers were made redundant in August 2024, including 291 underground workers, 73 administrative and office staff and 71 surface workers. Only those who had already earned the right to retire by 1 July 2024 lost their jobs. Employees of the Polish Mining Group (Polska Grupa Górnicza) made redundant represent 1.03 per cent of the company's total underground workforce, 3.6 per cent of the office and administrative workforce and 1.1 per cent of the surface workforce.The number of people who may be covered by the planned voluntary departure programme is not yet known.
Target groups: Employees in standard employment; Older people in employment (aged 55+)
Views of social partners: For the time being, the position of the trade unions operating in the Polish Mining Group regarding the voluntary departure programme is not known.

Title: Programme to retrain miners as technicians for the wind power industry
Title (national language): Program przekwalifikowywania się górników na techników dla energetyki wiatrowej
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Subcategory: Active labour market policies (enhancing employability, training, subsidised job creation, etc.)
Background information: The 'Wind - a mine of opportunities' project initiated by EDF Renewables Poland, aims to help miners and other workers leaving the mining sector to acquire skills and knowledge that will enable them to change careers and become competent in the operation and maintenance of onshore wind farms. The programme is a response to the growing demand for workers in the renewable energy sector. It is being delivered in partnership with training company Vulcan Training & Consultancy and Mine Restructuring Company (Polish: Spółka Restrukturyzacji Kopalń)
Content of measure: The 'Wind - a mine of opportunities' (Polish: Wiatr - kopalnia możliwości) project, led by EDF Renewables Poland, aims to help miners and other workers leaving the mining sector acquire the skills and knowledge needed to change careers and become qualified in the operation and maintenance of onshore wind farms.Training takes place at Vulcan Training & Consultancy in Szczecin, Poland. The full cost is covered by EDF, with accommodation and meals provided to participants. Workers are recruited from among the staff of phased-out coal mines in Poland, overseen by the Mine Restructuring Company (Polish: Spółka Restrukturyzacji Kopalń). Upon completion, trainees receive internationally recognized qualifications enabling them to work in the wind energy sector. The programme is comprehensive and accredited by the Global Wind Organisation (GWO), allowing graduates to take up roles in the installation and maintenance of wind turbines both in Poland and abroad. The training also complies with standards set by Poland’s Office of Technical Inspection (UDT).Participants receive instruction in safe working at height, fire safety, first aid, operation of mobile platforms and cranes, as well as hydraulics, mechanics, electrical systems, and bolting. The closure of coal mines will be accompanied by the creation of new jobs in renewable energy production, enabling former miners to remain in employment
Use of measure: The programme aims to retrain 60 miners from Silesian mines by the end of 2026, with a target of 10 participants per year. By February 2025, four two-week training sessions had been completed, during which a total of 35 individuals were trained. Each of them subsequently received a job offer from EDF Renewables. Since 2023, a total of 250 candidates have applied to the programme and undergone a recruitment process.
Views of social partners: Due to the absence of formal consultations and the limited scale of the programme, mining trade unions have not taken an official position on the matter.
Sectors: B5 Mining of coal and lignite
Occupations: Labourers in mining, construction, manufacturing and transport

Title: Malta's sustainable development strategy for 2050
Title (national language): L-Istrateġija ta’ Malta għall-Iżvilupp Sostenibbli għall-2050
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: Malta's Sustainable Development Vision for 2050 was adopted in September 2018. This vision was translated into a strategic policy by means of 'Malta's Sustainable Development Strategy for 2050' which was developed during 2022 and 2023 by means of consultations with all Government Ministries and their respective Sustainable Development Focal Points as well as private sector representatives and other NGOs. This process led to the strategy document being published in August 2024.
Content of measure: The strategic plan has five goals. The first goal is to transition towards a climate-neutral green and blue economy. The second goal is the preservation of sustainable urban development and cultural heritage. Strategic goal three is ensuring healthy lives and well-being for all. Goal four is accelerating digital transformation, smart mobility and connectivity. Goal five is achieving social fairness and prosperity for all. Each of these goals is broken down into several other objectives. The first goal related to the green and blue economy includes five objectives: towards a resilient and climate-neutral economy; sustainable consumption and production patterns which safeguard environmental and socio-economic wellbeing; protecting, conserving and enhancing natural capital resources to improve ecological resilience and sustainability; developing sustainable food systems to achieve food security and ensure environmental and socio-economic welfare; investing in sustainable finance for a greener and climate neutral economy. In terms of the second goal which regards urban development and cultural heritage, three goals are listed: placing cultural and heritage at the heart of the development of our local communities; sustainable urban planning and development of liveable and resilient towns and villages; sustainable demographic development for the creation of resilient communities. The third strategic goal has to do with health and wellbeing and contains two objectives: fostering good health for all by strengthening our public health system; and promoting good nutrition and active lifestyles for a healthy society.  Goal four deals with digital transformation and includes three objectives: towards a digitally empowered economy and society; building sustainable communities through smart mobility and connectivity; and investing in research and innovation for sustainable growth. The final goal deals with social fairness and prosperity and includes five objectives: empowering individuals and communities through policy instruments and measures for the benefit of all; ensuring accessible products, services and environments which address the needs of a diverse and changing population; building safer communities and ensuring timely and effective justice system; achieving high-quality education responsive to labour market needs; equal opportunities and access to fair, safe and secure working environments. Targets and indicators for each of these goals have been developed. Each of these goals will be translated into concrete actions in the next phase of the strategy, which will be Malta's Sustainable Development Action Plan for 2030.
Use of measure: No information
Actors: National government; Trade unions; Employers' organisations; Other social actors (e.g. NGOs)
Views of social partners: News reports suggested that several employer and trade unions alike were positive about the plan. The Malta Chamber provided detailed feedback about the plan as well as providing suggestions for its implementation. The Malta Chamber conducted its own consultation with industries and businesses from various sectors from its three economic groups, 17 Business Sections, its 11 Thematic Committees and Young Chamber Network. Many of the Chamber's views about the strategic policy related to the future implementation of the strategy highlighting the need for binding policies, good governance, establishing national progress and development indicators for both the economy and environment, and effective public stakeholder participation. The UHM Voice of the Workers provided some criticism regarding the perceived skirting of the issue regarding population growth, stating that current unsustainable population growth was not tackled, whilst at the same time noting that the policy stated that employers would be supported in bringing foreign workers to Malta. The union argued that this would not aid sustainability.

Title: Manifesto ‘Work and Energy for a Sustainable Transition’
Title (national language): Manifesto “Lavoro ed Energia per una transizione sostenibile”
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Subcategory: Active labour market policies (enhancing employability, training, subsidised job creation, etc.)
Background information: The "Labour and Energy for a Sustainable Transition" manifesto was introduced in November 2021 as Italy worked to meet the EU Green Deal's climate targets. The document addresses the significant challenge of increasing the country's annual CO2 reduction from 3 Mt to over 16 Mt, while ensuring job protection and maintaining industrial competitiveness.The initiative works within Italy's existing National Integrated Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC) and National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), following the framework established by EU Regulation 2021/1119 (European Climate Law) and its 55% emissions reduction target for 2030. The manifesto brings together industry stakeholders, unions and institutions to develop a practical approach to managing the social and economic aspects of energy transition through the current decade.
Content of measure: The manifesto outlines a comprehensive approach to Italy's energy transition, requiring an estimated investment of 1,100 billion euros through 2030 and aiming to create 250,000 new jobs in the energy sector. The initiative targets both existing workforce protection and future employment development.The measure establishes a coordinated framework involving universities, research institutions, industry, unions, and public authorities. It focuses on multiple decarbonisation solutions, including renewable energy sources, low-carbon technologies, and circular economy practices. An integrated and synergic approach with the contribution of all the energy sectors makes it possible to maintain and strengthen the current employment structure of the energy sector (around 515,000 direct and indirect jobs and a potential allied industry of around 300,000) and also to guarantee the important employment levels of other sectors, such as Hard to Abate and Automotive (with around 1,000,000 jobs), in which the energy component becomes decisive in providing competitive levers and solutions for decarbonisation.Key support mechanisms include a special public transition fund, financial support for vulnerable consumers through social tariffs and efficiency incentives, alongside industrial support through regulatory simplification and tax adjustments for low-carbon technologies.
Use of measure: Since these are recommendations of the social partners, there is no data on the implementation.
Actors: National government; Social partners jointly; Other social actors (e.g. NGOs)
Views of social partners: Broad support for the measure from all social partners involved. The manifesto represents a consensus document signed by industry associations (Confindustria Energia), major trade unions (CGIL, CISL, UIL), and consumer organisations.

Title: Enel’s ‘Statute of the Person'
Title (national language): Lo 'Statuto della Persona' di Enel
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Subcategory: Active labour market policies (enhancing employability, training, subsidised job creation, etc.)
Background information: Enel, Italy's multinational energy company, developed its participatory management system in response to the challenges of energy transition and the need for sustainable business transformation. The approach was formalised through a series of bipartite collective bargaining agreements, starting with the 2012 Protocol on National Industrial Relations. The regulatory framework is built upon agreements between Enel and three major Italian trade union federations (FILCTEM-CGIL, FLAEI-CISL and UILTEC-UIL), culminating in the 2022 "Statute of the Person"
Content of measure: The initiative comprises multiple interconnected agreements focusing on workforce management during the energy transition. The cornerstone measures include the 'Futur-e' project, involving the reconversion of 23 thermoelectric power plants and a mining area, alongside comprehensive workforce management strategies. Key provisions include employee redeployment, reskilling programmes, and early retirement schemes.The 2022 "Statute of the Person" establishes three primary areas of intervention: well-being and productivity measures, continuous learning initiatives, and safety protocols. The framework extends beyond Enel's direct employees to encompass the entire supply chain ecosystem.The agreements emphasise maintaining salary levels during transitions and providing comprehensive training and development opportunities.
Use of measure: The measures apply to Enel's workforce of approximately 70,000 employees across its operations, with provisions extending to external contractors and suppliers.
Views of social partners: Trade unions generally expressed strong support for Enel's initiatives, particularly the 2022 Statute of the Person. Union leaders' statements reflect positive reception: FILCTEM praised it as "concrete inclusive bargaining" that extends beyond direct employees to the supplier ecosystem. FLAEI-CISL described it as creating "broad and concrete prospects for shared growth" and commended Enel's "revolutionary evolution". UILTEC endorsed it as an "innovative agreement" focused on individual wellbeing. The only noted criticism was regarding the 'Futur-e' plan, where unions expressed concerns about "lack of sufficient information", though this project was ultimately acknowledged as successful.
Sectors: D35 Electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply

Title: Supporting the development of electromobility in Slovaki
Title (national language): Podpora rozvoja elektromobility na Slovensku
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: The Slovak government considers it necessary to adopt new policies and introduce measures that will strengthen the development of zero-emission mobility in Slovakia. On February 8, 2024, business associations in the automotive and transport sector called on the Slovak government to support both car manufacturers and those who will buy zero-emission vehicles - i.e. companies and individuals. They call for the accelerated implementation of programmes that have already been approved in the Action Plan for the Development of Electromobility. Money from the Recovery and Resilience Plan can be used to finance them (for example, those originally intended to support the decarbonization of the industry in the Košice steelworks in the amount of €300 million). On February 29, 2024, the Slovak government approved a resolution on the sustainability of automobile production in the Slovak Republic in the context of the transition to electric vehicle production and on selected problems of the development of electromobility.
Content of measure: The Ministry of Economy has developed a strategic Action Plan for the Development of Electromobility in the Slovak Republic (Government Resolution No. 306/2023). The implementation of measures has helped the development of electromobility in the Slovak Republic, in particular by implementing subsidy calls to support the purchase of electric vehicles, as well as supporting the construction of publicly accessible charging stations. Thanks to the measures taken, the building a battery ecosystem (environmental battery production) in Slovakia has been started through IPCEI projects (Important Projects of Common European Interest) accelerated depreciation of electric vehicles and the use of green vehicle registration plates for BEVs (battery electric vehicles) and PHEVs (plug-in hybrid electric vehicles) have been introduced.In 2024, there were approximately 2,600 charging points in Slovakia within the publicly accessible charging infrastructure (in 2030, an increase to over 6,500 is expected). The resolution of the government of the Slovak Republic (122/2024) on the Revised Action Plan for the Development of Electromobility sets specific tasks for all ministries.
Use of measure: The "Call for Support for the Construction of Charging Infrastructure for Electric Vehicles for Local Governments and Organisations Established by Them (Call Code 03I04-26-V01) - Amendment" is currently published on the website of the Ministry of Economy. The total indicative amount of the mechanism's funds allocated for this call is €10,236,000 excluding VAT.
Views of social partners: Employers initiated a proposal to increase the government's support for the development of electromobility. The government has not yet adopted a resolution on more massive support
Sectors: C27 Manufacture of electrical equipment; C29 Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers; D35 Electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply

Title: ‘Future collective agreement’ at Bosch Mobility
Title (national language): Zukunftstarifvertrag bei Bosch Mobility
Category: Protection of workers, adaptation of workplace
Background information: The IG Metall trade union has concluded a "future collective agreement" with Bosch Mobility to secure the company's future in the transformation process. Bosch Mobility is one of the largest suppliers for the automotive sector and therefore strongly affected by the challenges of the green transition. The agreement includes measures to increase the involvement of employees and the works council in the company's economic and strategic planning. In addition, it has been agreed that there will be no compulsory redundancies until the end of 2027, ensuring financial stability for employees. The collective agreement came into force at the beginning of 2024.
Content of measure: The "future collective agreement" negotiated by IG Metall and Bosch Mobility aims to secure the company's future in the green transformation process. To this end, measures have been agreed to actively involve employees in forward-looking planning. This means that the works councils are involved at an early stage in strategic and economic planning, for example in the selection of locations where a new product will be manufactured (e.g. in connection with e-mobility and hydrogen) and in the development of guiding principles for the future direction of the company. At all German sites covered by the collective bargaining agreement, annual goal-setting processes are to be carried out with the involvement of the works councils and employees, so that they can contribute ideas for shaping the future and help develop concepts. The parties also agreed to rule out compulsory redundancies until the end of 2027.
Use of measure: The collective agreement is applicable to 80,000 employees at all Bosch Mobility locations in Germany.
Views of social partners: The responses of the social partners to the proposed 'Future Collective Agreement' are, for the most part, positive and supportive. The employers' side places considerable emphasis on the importance of the agreement for the strengthening of the social partnership, and regards cooperation with the trade unions as being of the utmost importance for competitiveness and the shaping of the future. IG Metall welcomes the outcome of the negotiations as an important step towards ensuring the future viability of the company and the security of its employees. However, it emphasises the necessity of a detailed elaboration of the agreed measures. Both parties acknowledge the significance of shared accountability and collaboration in the transformation of Bosch Mobility.
Sectors: C29 Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers

Title: Regional transformation network for the vehicle and supplier industry Berlin Brandenburg (ReTraNetz-BB)
Title (national language): Regionale Transformationsnetzwerk für die Fahrzeug- und Zulieferindustrie Berlin Brandenburg (ReTraNetz-BB)
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: The regional transformation network for the vehicle and supplier industry in Berlin-Brandenburg (ReTraNetz-BB) supports the vehicle industry in the region, which is currently undergoing profound change. The project aims to support SMEs in Berlin-Brandenburg in the transformation to CO2-neutral mobility and production, promote existing strengths, develop new topics and devise measures. It should not only benefit the vehicle and supplier industry, but also deliver results that are transferable to other sectors and contexts. The project serves to secure relevant future fields of the automotive industry in the region and promotes the preservation and expansion of added value and jobs. Members of the network include various stakeholders from educational institutions, science and business development as well as the IG Metall trade union and the Association of the Metal and Electrical Industry.
Content of measure: ReTraNetz-BB offers a wide range of measures to effectively support the transformation of the vehicle and supplier industry in Berlin-Brandenburg. A central focus is on the qualification, retraining and further training of skilled workers. The network develops and promotes practical concepts, helps to identify training needs and supports companies with examples of best practice. It assists in the testing and evaluation of measures to ensure that have a lasting effect.ReTraNetz-BB also initiates long-term cooperation and networks between science and industry. In this way, technological core competences and results from research projects can be transferred into innovative solutions for industry. The range of services also includes arranging funding opportunities in areas such as digitalisation, coaching, investment, research and development, energy optimisation and internationalisation.To develop new business models, the network promotes dialogue through expert discussions and workshops, with a particular focus on digital business models and the circular economy. The "real world laboratory" at the Production Technology Centre Berlin serves as a central location for testing innovative process chains and transferring sustainable technologies into real-life application scenarios.
Use of measure: There are no evaluation results yet.
Actors: Social partners jointly; Trade unions; Employers' organisations; Company / Companies; Other social actors (e.g. NGOs)
Target groups: Sector specific set of companies; SMEs
Views of social partners: The social partners support the ReTraNetz-BB and see transformation as a key task for the future. IG Metall stresses the importance of mobilising the expertise of all stakeholders and welcomes the cooperation within the network. The Association of the Metal and Electrical Industry expects ReTraNetz-BB to accelerate the networking of industrial companies with the digital economy in order to promote technical innovations and new business models. Overall, the network is seen as an important instrument for jointly exploiting the opportunities of transformation.
Sectors: C24 Manufacture of basic metals; C25 Manufacture of fabricated metal products, except machinery and equipment; C27 Manufacture of electrical equipment; C28 Manufacture of machinery and equipment n.e.c.; C29 Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers
Occupations: Metal, machinery and related trades workers

Title: Proposals of IME GSEVEE for the Transition to the Post-Lignite Era in the Region of Western Macedonia: A Holistic Social, Economic, and Environmental Framework
Title (national language): Προτάσεις του ΙΜΕ ΓΣΕΒΕΕ  για τη μετάβαση στη μεταλιγνιτική εποχή της Περιφέρειας Δυτικής Μακεδονίας.Ένα ολιστικό, κοινωνικό, οικονομικό και περιβαλλοντικό πλαίσι
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: The Research Institute of Hellenic Confederation of Professionals, Craftsmen and Merchants (IME GSEVEE) published in May 2021 a research document titled “Proposals for the Transition to the Post-Lignite Era in the Region of Western Macedonia: A Holistic Social, Economic, and Environmental Framework.” This text served as GSEVEE’s contribution to the public consultation on the Territorial Just Transition Plan (TJTP) of Western Macedonia. It aimed to present a realistic and actionable program for the region's restoration, guided by a unified approach that integrates nature, economy, and human well-being.The document transfers international expertise, identifies contradictions and weaknesses in existing projects, and ultimately proposes solutions for the post-decarbonization era. It also provides an overview of the Just Development Transition (JDT) Plan as it was presented for consultation in October 2020, analyzing its strengths and pinpointing areas of ambiguity or potential future challenges.
Content of measure: In the 2021 research document by IME GSEVEE, the proposals for the Economic Rehabilitation of Western Macedonia focused on nine key guidelines:*strengthening and transforming primary production; *promoting the processing of primary production; *marketing - promoting sales and creating branded products; *strengthening infrastructures; *providing incentives for voluntary associations and synergies (clusters); *supporting agricultural production;*strengthening the educational level to overcome the chronic lag of the region; *supporting incomes to act as a safety net for those who do not enter the labour market on time, and finally; *continuously assessing the results so that lignite phase-out and greenhouse gas neutrality are both socially neutral and not accompanied by a social burden. For these proposals to succeed, agreeing on the number of people affected by decarbonization is essential. If only one measure were implemented, creating a scientific and profes-sional hub (clusters) to establish a single brand for Western Macedonia would be ideal. This could boost all sectors and address existing challenges. Additionally, the current decarboni-zation timetable is extremely and unjustifiably violent.and must must be extended in time and follow the EU’s timetable, which provides for greenhouse gas neutrality by 2050.
Use of measure: There is no available information regarding the influence of GSEVEE's proposals on the design and implementation of the Just Transition program
Views of social partners: The initiative described is solely an independent action undertaken by GSEVEE, a social partner representing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).There are no other social partner's reactions to the measure

Title: KHUL - skills, sustainable development, learning
Title (national language): KHUL - Kompetens, hållbar utveckling, lärande
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: As part of the just transition fund, the mineral company Boliden Mineral has received financing from the managing authority The Swedish Agency for Economic and Regional Growth to re- and upskill their workforce to realise the green transition in the mineral industry. The project aims to upskill the existing workforce to adapt to the technological advancement in the copper smelting factory in Rönnskär. The funding application was submitted in September, 2023.
Content of measure: Boliden Mineral has allocated SEK 34 million (€2,95 million) to the project, 50% of which is financed by the company. The focus is preparing the workforce for automation processes, digitalisation, and new methods of working. The project constructs a "digital twin" in which workers at the company receive on-the-job training for the new working methods. The simulation is used for employees to experiment and learn new skills such as overhead crane driving in a safe environment.The project is conducted within a wider framework of modernising the copper smelting plant. The goals are to prepare the factory for the EU energy- and climate targets in 2030 and the Paris climate accords, as well as contributing to a safer workplace and sustainable working conditions.
Use of measure: There is no information on exactly how many workers participate in the project, but the factory itself employs 860 workers. According to Boliden’s press release, the funding is sufficient to meet every employee’s need and will for skill development.
Actors: National government; Company / Companies; EU (Council, EC, EP)
Views of social partners: IF Metall, the trade union representing the workers at Boliden Mineral AB has written about the Just Transition Funds in a positive light. They say that the funds enable companies to take decisions that help their members with their future in the industry, and that the existence of the funds has highlighted the issue of upskilling in the green transition. The shortage of labour in the north of Sweden has also placed an emphasis on upskilling the existing workforce rather than hiring new labour to replace the former workers. The employer organisation Industriarbetsgivarna are similarly positive to the measure, which enables one of their large members to upskill their workforce.
Sectors: C24 Manufacture of basic metals
Occupations: Labourers in mining, construction, manufacturing and transport

Title: Study by INE GSEE on Just Transition in Greece
Title (national language): Μελέτη του ΙΝΕ ΓΣΕΕ για τη Δίκαιη μετάβαση στην Ελλάδα
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Subcategory: Active labour market policies (enhancing employability, training, subsidised job creation, etc.)
Background information: The Research Institute of Greek General Confederation of Labour (INE GSEE) published a study in 2021, titled "Just Transition in the Greek Reality within the Framework of the EU."This study examines European and international transition policies, Greece's current situation, and offers policy recommendations. It highlights the need for climate justice, inclusive dialogue, and safeguarding workers, emphasizing that a just workforce transition is crucial. Greek trade unions, concerned about the rapid post-lignite shift, stress the importance of protecting jobs, reskilling workers, and meaningful social dialogue, often lacking in Greece. They support a green economy that ensures employment and adapts workers' skills to new demands.
Content of measure: The INE GSEE study on just transition highlights severe impacts on Kozani, Florina, and Megalopolis, where lignite plants operate, including rising unemployment and economic decline. Local trade unions argue that the rapid decarbonisation process will worsen these issues and de-mand an extension of lignite plant operations to ensure a smoother tran-sition while prioritizing job and income protection.GENOP-DEI, representing PPC workers, also criticizes the rushed timetable, warning of its negative effects on workers and local economies. They stress that the consultation on the JDT master plan was insufficient and advocate for more time to mitigate adverse outcomes.To address these challenges, the study proposes policy measures such as new fiscal tools, support for affected regions, loans and state guarantees, cluster development, and stronger cooperation among stakeholders to achieve a just transition.
Use of measure: No information is available on the impact of INE GSEE's proposals on the design and implementation of the Just Transition program.
Views of social partners: There are no other social partner's reactions to the measure
Regions: EL531 Γρεβενά, Κοζάνη (Grevena, Kozani); EL533 Φλώρινα (Florina); EL651 Αργολίδα, Αρκαδία (Argolida, Arkadia)

Title: Adult education for the metal industry and green transition
Title (national language): Yrkesvux för metallindustrin och den gröna omställningen
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Subcategory: Active labour market policies (enhancing employability, training, subsidised job creation, etc.)
Background information: Skellefteå municipality in the region of Västerbotten region in the north of Sweden has applied for funding from the Just Transition Funds to develop customised traning courses and increase their adult education capacity in the region. The specific aim is to train the future workforce for the new green steel and metal factories that is key to the green transition in Sweden.
Content of measure: The measure aims to better match workers with the needs of the metal industry employers in the region, throughout the value chain. The project aims to coordinate the local actors to provide a more well suited adult vocational training to the local metal industry employers, either by creating new vocational training programmes or adapting existing training programmes. The project has recieved SEK 20 million (€ 1,73 million), with an additional SEK 1,9 million (approx. € 165,000) from Skellefteå municipality and SEK 300,000 (€ 26,000) from the Västerbotten region. Beyond creating new adult vocational training programmes, the funds should also cover the purchasing of new educational equipment and train the educators at the adult vocational training providers.
Use of measure: Use of measure not yet known.
Views of social partners: IF Metall, the main trade union for steel and metal workers, has previously criticised employers for not investing in training for their workers, and have historically called for more vocational training to meet the demands of the green and digital transitions.
Sectors: B7 Mining of metal ores; B9 Mining support service activities; C24 Manufacture of basic metals

Title: Together - Eni Industrial Relations Model
Title (national language): Insieme - Modello di relazioni industriali Eni
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Subcategory: Active labour market policies (enhancing employability, training, subsidised job creation, etc.)
Background information: This protocol was established in late 2020 amid increasing pressures for energy transition and COVID-19 disruptions. ENI, a multinational oil and gas company, needed to adapt its business model to meet EU Green Deal requirements while maintaining employment and competitiveness levels during a volatile period for energy markets.The regulatory framework includes Italian Law 81/2017 (Article 19.1) governing smart working and worker disconnection rights, ILO standards for global maternity protection (implemented by ENI since 2015), and EU Sustainable Development Scenario requirements for emission reductions.This agreement between ENI and major Italian unions (Filctem CGIL, Femca CISL, Uiltec UIL) provides a comprehensive framework for managing energy transition while protecting worker rights, particularly significant as it was signed during the pandemic when work arrangements were rapidly evolving.
Content of measure: The protocol "INSIEME" establishes comprehensive coverage for ENI's workforce transformation, encompassing both ENI SpA employees and those in controlled companies. The measures span across multiple areas of employment and welfare support.The coverage includes smart working arrangements with different tiers: general office workers can work remotely one day per week, while parents of children with disabilities get two days. New parents and employees with serious health conditions also receive enhanced flexibility in their working arrangements.The scale of support is substantial, with the company fully covering basic healthcare plans through Fasie (Fondo Assistenza Sanitaria Integrativa Energia, is the supplementary healthcare fund for energy sector workers) and Faschim (Fondo di Assistenza Sanitaria, is the supplementary healthcare fund for chemical sector workers) enrollment, plus additional contributions based on employee-selected coverage levels. The company commits significant resources to training, with 1.5 million hours dedicated to HSE (Health, Safety and Environment) topics over four years.Financial commitments include an annual investment of over 2 billion euros in asset integrity (this refers to ENI's systems and processes designed to ensure the safe, reliable operation of its physical infrastructure throughout their entire lifecycle), full salary coverage for 10 days of paternity leave, and extensive digital transformation investments. The company also provides various welfare benefits including summer camps for employees' children, school orientation services, and elderly care support programs.Many benefits aren't quantified in monetary terms.
Use of measure: Currently, about 4,500 employees have voluntarily joined the organisational smart working programme. In terms of specific operational areas, around 2,300 people work across all business lines supporting asset integrity functions. The initial digital transformation training programme completed in October 2019 reached about 3,700 employees from various departments.Looking forward, the company's retail customer base is projected to grow to over 20 million by 2050. Healthcare coverage through Fasie and Faschim is provided automatically to all employees, though specific enrollment numbers aren't detailed.One significant example is the Digital Lighthouse project at the COVA (Centro Olio Val d'Agri) facility, which was chosen as ENI's first fully digitalized plant. This implementation included Virtual Reality Training systems that allow operators to practice safety scenarios in immersive environments that simulate real conditions with visual and sound effects.
Funding: Companies; National Recovery and Resilience Facility
Views of social partners: Based on the protocol document, the trade unions (Filctem CGIL, Femca CISL, Uiltec UIL) express strongly supportive views of the measures. This is evident in their joint press release where union leaders Marco Falcinelli, Nora Garofalo, and Paolo Pirani state that the protocol will help govern energy transition.
Sectors: D35 Electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply

Title: SSAB Academy
Title (national language): SSAB Academy
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Subcategory: Active labour market policies (enhancing employability, training, subsidised job creation, etc.)
Background information: The state owned steel enterprise SSAB has applied for and received financing from the Just Transition Funds for an internal vocational training academy project for electricians. The Swedish steel giant aims to electrify their entire operation, and transform their production processes to produce green steel. The planned changes in Luleå will lead to a reduction of CO2 emissions of about 2.8 million tonnes annually, a reduction of about 90% compared to current operations
Content of measure: The SSAB Academy is an internal education platform for the entire SSAB company. They launched two pilot training programmes in autumn of 2023, one for educating existing workers into certified electricians and one in leadership focused on change. The electrician programme is launched in order for SSAB to becomne self-sufficient in their demand for certified electricians. The SSAB Academy fast tracks the electric worker education. The programme is a total of 27 weeks, with 15 weeks of education, and then 12 weeks of practical training, during which the permanently employed electricians act as supervisors. The project has a budget of SEK 40 million (approx. € 3,5 million).
Use of measure: In January of 2024 SSAB started by educating 10 workers to become electricians, with about 20 already certified electricans acting as supervisors
Target groups: Employees in standard employment; Other businesses
Views of social partners: IF Metall has stated that the education is of high quality, and that students knowledge is rigoursly tested to ensure safety of the trained electricians. However, some employed electricians have voiced concern for the measure, stating that the education is too short to learn all the necessary electrical skills to safely work as an electrician after only 27 weeks. According to an article in Norrländska Socialdemokraten, NSD, around 50-electricians have petitioned the union to be more critical of the measure, which they also argue contributes to keeping wages lower by training unqualified workers as electricians.
Sectors: C24 Manufacture of basic metals; C25 Manufacture of fabricated metal products, except machinery and equipment

Title: Climate ambassadors
Title (national language): Uppdrag: Klimatambassadör
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: The background to this measure is that the trade unions want to work to influence their workplaces to better adapt to the green transition. The initiative was initiated by the trade unions IF Metall and Unionen, the staffing agency Adecco, the business organisation CirEko, the government agency Vinnova and the Stockholm Resilience Centre.
Content of measure: The Climate Ambassador role is a role for trade union members. To become a climate ambassador in the workplace the worker better advocate for their workplace to make adaptations for the green transition. To become a climate ambassador, the worker can participate in training modules. The first module is an e-learning course called Klimatnyfiken (transl. Climate curious). The second module is a series of workshops, with three individual components. These are focused on what the workplace can do, that saving the jobs will also contribute to saving the climate and how to maintain a hopeful outlook as a climate ambassador. The workshops are intended to be done together with colleagues at the workplace.Finally, there is a compendium available for more in-depth information. The measure is financed by the government agency for innovation, Vinnova. The original project ran from June 2022 to November 2024, but the modules are still available (on June, 2025). The initial project funding from Vinnova amounted to over SEK 1,4 million (€127,000).
Use of measure: The initial project had 450 people participating in the online courses. Vinnova expects that the publicly available material will reach over 2,000 potential climate ambassadors.
Actors: National government; Trade unions; Company / Companies
Views of social partners: IF Metall commented when launching the initiative that their jobs as local trade union representatives needs to be a part of the new industrial revolution, as they call it.
Sectors: C24 Manufacture of basic metals; C25 Manufacture of fabricated metal products, except machinery and equipment

Title: Expert group to support the creation of the Territorial Just Transition Plan in South-Ostrobothnia
Title (national language): Etelä-Pohjanmaan alueellisen siirtymäsuunnitelman asiantuntijäryhmä
Status of regulation: New aspects included into existing measure
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: A part of Finland’s Just Transition Fund-strategy is to halve the energy use of peat by 2030. The South Ostrobothnia region is one of the most significant peat regions in Finland, contributing to 25% of all energy peat production areas in the country. The region’s regional cooperation group [Maakunnan yhteistyöryhmä], which monitors the implementation of all EU structural fund programmes regionally, set an expert group to support the creation of the Territorial Just Transition Plan.
Content of measure: The group consisted of the regional council, the ELY-centre (regional centers responsible for the regional implementation and development tasks of the central government), businesses, energy companies, regional environmental organisations and forestry organisations, forest owners, institutes of education, research institutions, as well as the Employers' Trade Association of Finnish Forestry and Earth-Moving Contractors [Koneyrittäjät] and the Entrepreneurs of South-Ostrobothnia [Etelä-Pohjanmaan Yrittäjät] (the branch organisation of Finnish Entrepreneurs [Yrittäjät]).The purpose of the expert group was to inform the planning process, engage stakeholders in the objectives of the plan, and disseminate information, as it was recognised that the Territorial Just Transition Plan required broad involvement of interest groups.The expert group was active from fall 2020 to spring 2021. No information is available regarding renumeration for participants.
Use of measure: The Territorial Just Transition Plan for the South Ostrobothnia region was approved by the European Commission on 16 December 2022.
Actors: Employers' organisations; Other social actors (e.g. NGOs); Local / regional government
Target groups: Other groups of workers; Other businesses
Views of social partners: Involved in the measure.
Sectors: B8 Other mining and quarrying

Title: Alliance for a just transition Sweden (ARK)
Title (national language): Allians för rättvis klimatomställning (ARK)
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: The Alliance for a just transition Sweden started after being inspired by the European Alliance For A Just Transition. The cooperative organisation has 51 members from various parts of the civil society, including trade unions, climate organisations, activist organisations, NGOs and the Sami parliament. The group is not bound to any political party, and is working to increase the focus on the just transition. The purpose is to bring together the environmental movement and organisations working for human, economic and social rights behind a common agenda for a just climate transition.To build public opinion for a more ambitious and equitable Swedish climate policy, in line with science and the Paris Agreement principles of global justice.
Content of measure: The alliance has made seven demands on the government. 1. To increase the pace of the green transition. 2. Improve the governance and coordination of the work towards the green transition3. Include citizens and people in work by giving transparency and influence. 4. Work for climate justice5. Safeguard workers in Sweden 6. Invest in the transition. 7. Support a fair climate transition internationally. The demands include a call for cooperation between trade unions in different sectors to increase the dialogue between employers at the workplace level. They encourage unions putting pressure on the employers to draw up plans for how to conduct a just transition. The demands also focus on inclusivity of people, such as the Sami people, and their rights to make decisions about their own land.
Use of measure: The cooperation is ongoing, and they have voiced their seven demands to the government, but it has not yet become part of any government plan.In the spring of 2024, ARK's EU Working Group organised a series of interviews with candidates in the EU parliament election with the theme of how they will work for a just climate transition.As of June, 2025, there are 51 alliance member organistaions.
Actors: Trade unions; Other social actors (e.g. NGOs)
Views of social partners: Not applicable

Title: Agreement on vocational training and qualifications
Title (national language): Acordo sobre formação profissional e qualificação
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: The Agreement on vocational training and qualifications: a strategic goal for people, companies and the country was signed between the government and the social partners on 28 July 2021, in the Standing Committee for Social Dialogue.This tripartite Agreement aims at reinforcing vocational training and qualifications in Portugal, notably in order to fulfil the target of achieving 60% annual participation of adults in education and training by 2030, and considering the digital and green transitions.
Content of measure: Considering: (a) the growing centrality of competences, vocational training and qualification for people, workers and companies in contemporary societies and contemporary societies and economies and the need to strengthen and modernise the vocational the need to strengthen and modernise the vocational training system and access to lifelong learning for companies, workers and citizens to lifelong learning; (b) the need to act to fulfil the target of achieving 60% annual participation of adults in education and training by 2030; (c) the recognition of the importance of vocational training and qualifications for public policies is expressed in the incorporation of this dimension in several of the sectoral strategic planning instruments in the context of public policies, namely in the National Energy and Climate Plan 2030, the National Strategy for National Hydrogen Strategy, in the Long-Term Strategy for Building Renewal; (d) the profound transformations in labour and markets, including the digital energy transition and climate action, which reinforce the centrality and importance of training and require an acceleration in the need to acquire and deepen and deepening of competences in order to better adapt to technological and organisational technological and organisational changes.A solid commitment to vocational training and qualification is a fundamental factor in one of the country's deepest deficits, to improve people's opportunities and life people's life opportunities and prospects, with an impact on social cohesion, and to leverage the competitiveness of companies and the Portuguese economy. Therefore, the government and the social partners (with the exception of CGTP-IN) signed this tripartite Agreement.
Use of measure: This does not apply.
