Background information: The Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Protection (BMWK) is promoting the conversion to highly energy-efficient refrigeration and air conditioning systems as part of the Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Directive of the National Climate Protection Initiative (NKI). The amended directive has been in force since December 1, 2020, and was initially set to run for three years before being amended again on March 1, 2024. The measures supported contribute to increasing energy efficiency and reducing emissions of fluorinated greenhouse gases, thereby helping to achieve the German government's climate protection goals.
Content of measure: Funding is available for measures to increase energy efficiency in stationary refrigeration and air conditioning systems that use non-halogenated refrigerants in commercial applications. This also includes the installation of system components (e.g., for heat pump operation for waste heat recovery or storage tanks), provided that energy efficiency can be further increased. Eligible measures relate to the installation of systems, their retrofitting and conversion, and the efficiency conversion of small systems.Companies, non-profit organizations, municipalities, local authorities, special-purpose associations and municipal enterprises, universities and schools, hospitals and church institutions are eligible to apply, regardless of their profit motive. The subsidy calculator calculates the amount of possible funding based on the current funding guidelines. To do this, the calculator requests parameters and values that are relevant for the calculation, such as the type and cooling capacity of the refrigeration unit and the type and performance of the components of a refrigeration or air conditioning system.
Use of measure: Under the Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Directive, a total of around 5,200 highly energy-efficient refrigeration and air conditioning systems have been subsidized to date, with funding of almost €300 million. The subsidized systems can achieve energy savings of around 40 percent, thereby making a significant contribution to reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
Views of social partners: Various industry associations and manufacturers/specialist companies have issued a statement. The Association of German Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Companies (VDKF) and the Federal Technical College for Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Technology have drafted a statement, which has also been co-signed by BIV, FGK, BTGA, and the RLT Manufacturers' Association. In it, they call for the continuation of BAFA funding in accordance with the “Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Directive”.

Title: Environmental bonus for electric car
Title (national language): Umweltbonus E-Autos
Subcategory: Direct subsidies (full or partial) or damage compensation
Background information: The environmental bonus was introduced in July 2016 to support the spread of electric mobility in Germany and thus advance climate targets in the transport sector. The purchase of battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrids, and fuel cell vehicles was subsidized by a grant, half of which was paid by the federal government and half by manufacturers. The legal basis for this was the directive on promoting the sale of electric vehicles issued by the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWE) in June 2016. The subsidy was administered by the Federal Office for Economic Affairs and Export Control (BAFA). Over the years, the subsidy was adjusted several times, including with the 'innovation bonus' in 2020, and from 2023 onwards, the subsidy only applied to purely electric cars. Originally planned to run until the end of 2024, the environmental bonus was discontinued prematurely on December 17, 2023, due to the budget situation and following a ruling by the Federal Constitutional Court.
Content of measure: The environmental bonus for electric cars was aimed at private individuals, companies, foundations, corporations, and associations that purchased a new battery-electric vehicle, a fuel cell vehicle, or—until 2022—a plug-in hybrid vehicle. Only the purchase or leasing of new vehicles that were on the list of eligible models maintained by the Federal Office for Economic Affairs and Export Control (BAFA) was eligible for funding. A minimum holding period or leasing period was also required to avoid windfall effects.The subsidy consisted of a federal contribution and a mandatory manufacturer contribution. In the original scheme introduced in 2016, the government subsidy amounted to €2,000 for pure electric vehicles and €1,500 for plug-in hybrids, supplemented by the same manufacturer contribution. With the innovation bonus introduced in 2020, the federal share doubled, making up to €9,000 per vehicle possible. From 2023, the subsidy rates were gradually reduced before the subsidy was terminated prematurely on December 17, 2023. The environmental bonus was one of the central instruments for promoting electric mobility in Germany.
Use of measure: The use of the environmental bonus fluctuated considerably between 2016 and 2023, depending on the subsidy conditions. In the early years, relatively few vehicles received subsidies. However, with the introduction of the innovation premium in 2020, which doubled the federal government's share, the number of subsidies rose sharply: Between 2020 and 2022 alone, the majority of the total 2.17 million subsidized vehicles were accounted for, including 1.40 million battery electric vehicles (BEVs) and 0.77 million plug-in hybrids (PHEVs). From 2022 onwards, demand fell again as subsidies for PHEVs were restricted and finally completely abolished from 2023. At the same time, the subsidy rates for BEVs were reduced. In total, government subsidies of €10.17 billion and €5.28 billion in manufacturer contributions were approved.
Views of social partners: IG Metall supported the environmental bonus in principle, as it secured demand for electric cars and investments. However, it sharply criticized the abrupt end to the bonus in December 2023, which it believed destroyed planning security and further unsettled employees and companies in the automotive industry. It called for more reliable framework conditions.

Title: Increase to the vehicle tax on electric and hybrid cars

Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: The government of Finland has increased the tax on electric and hybrid vehicles through an amendment to the Act on vehicle tax 1281/2003 [Ajoneuvoverolaki]. The increase affects both basic vehicle tax [perusvero] and the tax on driving power in vehicle tax [käyttövoimavero].The amendment was presented as part of the 2025 budget proposal and is in line with the governments’ measures for fiscal balance. The government argues in their proposal that as the vehicle base in Finland has increasingly become electric, the tax incentives on these low-emission vehicles has harmed the tax base. The new tax criteria will come into force on January 1, 2026. As vehicle tax is calculated on a daily basis and levied in advance for a 12-month tax period per vehicle, vehicle tax bills sent during 2025 will already include tax levied in accordance with the 2026 regulations.
Content of measure: The basic vehicle tax for fully electric cars will increase by approximately €53 and the driving power tax by an average of approximately €35 per year. The basic tax on rechargeable hybrid cars will increase by an average of approximately €37 per year. The driving power tax on rechargeable gasoline-powered hybrids will increase by an average of approximately €41 per year. The driving power tax on rechargeable diesel-powered hybrids will decrease by an average of approximately €140 per year. The basic tax on low-emission non-rechargeable hybrid cars will increase by approximately €0–11 per year.Changes to vehicle tax are estimated to increase vehicle tax revenue by approximately €34 million in 2026.The government has simultaneously lowered the tax rate on older, higher emission vehicles (Case FI-2025-1/3922).
Use of measure: At the end of 2023, there were approximately 2, 756 million passenger cars and 340,000 vans in use. Of these, approximately 87,000 were electric vehicles and 135,000 were hybrid vehicles

Title: Light Vehicle Scrappage Incentive Programme

Background information: The 2024 State Budget (Law 82/2023), under Article 281, provided for the creation of a Light Vehicle Scrappage Incentive Programme, which ultimately was not implemented. It was only in 2025, with the publication of Notice AAC 02/2025 – Incentive for the introduction into circulation of zero-emission vehicles in 2025, that this programme came into effect.The programme is managed by the Environmental Fund (Fundo Ambiental), which is under the Ministry of the Environment of Portugal.

This support is not cumulative with other forms of funding. Eligible vehicles are defined as category M1 passenger cars, exclusively electric, whose first purchase and registration are made in the name of the beneficiary after 1 January 2025, either through a purchase and sale contract or a financial leasing agreement with a minimum duration of 24 months. Only vehicles with a final acquisition cost not exceeding €38,500, including VAT and associated expenses, are eligible, with this ceiling extended to €55,000 in the case of vehicles with more than five seats.The financial allocation of the Programme amounts to €8.7 million, of which €5.7 million is allocated to individuals and €3 million to entities, namely Private Institutions of Social Solidarity, Transport Authorities and Local Authorities.

Title: Photovoltaic Green House 2024 programme

Background information: The programme, established through the Ministry of Environment order no. 2045/2024, aims to finance the purchase and installation of photovoltaic panel systems that use renewable, nonpolluting energy sources for producing electricity, as well as for consumer use for consumers connected to the national electricity distribution network. Installations for storing electricity produced from renewable sources can also be purchased via this programme. The programme should increase energy efficiency, improve air quality, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions by photovoltaic panel systems with a minimum power of 3 kW to produce the electricity needed for own consumption, storage, and delivery of the surplus to the national energy system. The objective of the program is to increase the capacity for producing electricity from renewable sources and the amount of electricity produced from renewable sources. The indicator used in the program is performance indicator (I), the total amount of greenhouse gases (kg CO_2) reduced by installing photovoltaic panel systems, calculated over the entire project monitoring period.
Content of measure: The programme is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Water and Forests through the Environmental Fund Administration (AFM). Those who enroll in the programme can benefit from significant sums of money to cover a large part of the costs of their projects. The programme was relaunched in 2024 (it initially started in 2019 and has been renewed every two years), with a focus on financing photovoltaic systems to produce electricity from renewable sources. The applicant who is a natural person and who cumulatively meets some conditions as: has a permanent domicile or residence in Romania; has no outstanding obligations to the state budget and local budget, in accordance with the national legislation in force; is domiciled at the address where the project will be implemented or is the owner of the building. Funding is granted in the maximum amount for the purchase and installation of a photovoltaic panel system and a storage facility for electricity produced from renewable sources, provided that the beneficiary contributes 3,000 lei (approx. €600). If the total amount of the purchase and installation of a photovoltaic panel system is more than 33,000 lei (approx. €6,600), the beneficiary must cover from its own funds.

Title: Reduction of CO2 emissions in businesses

Status of regulation: New aspects included into existing measure

Background information: The programme, implemented by the Ministry of Development, Public Works and Administration (MDPWA), aims to increase the energy performance of residential buildings constructed before 31 December 2005, by reducing energy consumption for heating so that the specific annual energy consumption calculated for heating homes is below 100 kWh/m² of usable floor space. The programme aims to improve hygiene and thermal comfort conditions, reduce heat loss and energy consumption, reduce maintenance costs for heating and hot water consumption, reduce pollutant emissions generated by energy production, transport, and consumption, and preserve architectural, environmental, and chromatic integration values in the urban environment.The program is regulated by Government Emergency Ordinance No. 18/2009, with subsequent amendments and additions, and the Methodological Norms for the application of Government Emergency Ordinance No. 18/2009, approved by Order No. 625 of April 5, 2023.
Content of measure: Interventions provided through the program aim to increase the energy performance of apartment buildings constructed before 31 December 2005 through:•	thermal rehabilitation of the building,•	thermal rehabilitation of the heating system,•	rehabilitation and modernization of the heat distribution system,•	thermal rehabilitation works on the hot water supply system,•	installation and purchase, where appropriate, of alternative systems for producing energy from renewable sources,•	repair/replacement, where appropriate, of the electric drive mechanisms of passenger lifts, based on a specialist technical report.Funding for the interventions is provided as 60% from the state budget, within the limits of the funds allocated annually for this purpose in the MDPWA budget; 40% from funds approved annually for this purpose in local governgments' budgets and/or from other legally constituted sources.The share of the contribution of local public administration authorities is established based on socioeconomic criteria, within the limit of a maximum 30% of the value of the intervention, and is approved by decision of the local councils, respectively of the local councils of the sectors of Bucharest, as the case may be.The contribution share of the owners' association may not be less than 10% of the value of the intervention and is ensured by the association during the execution of the intervention, based on the work reports.By exception from the provisions of above prevision, the amounts advanced by the local public administration authorities to ensure the owners' association's own contribution (10%) is considered social expenses and shall not be recovered from the following categories of owners, natural people:•	people with disabilities or families with dependent people with disabilities,•	single people/families who, in the last 3 months prior to the social survey conducted by the local public administration authority, had average net monthly income per single person/family member below the average net wage (5,546 RON, approx. €1,100 for year 2024),•	war veterans and their surviving spouses,•	pensioners, regardless of their status, whose average monthly net income per person/family member is below the average net wage in the economy.
Use of measure: The total number of owners associations who will benefit from the multi annual program for 2024-2026 is 175. The total budget was 331 million RON (approx. €66,2) and the actual spending is 326 million RON (approx. €65,1)
Views of social partners: There is no publicly available information about the social partners' views or reaction on the measure.

Title: Preparation of the Social Climate Plan of the Republic of Bulgaria
Title (national language): Постановление № 24 от 8 април 2025 г. за организация и координация на подготовката на Социалния план за климата на Република България и за определяне на органите и структурите, отговорни за неговата подготовка и управление, и на техните основни функции
Background information: The decree defines the procedure for preparing the Social Climate Plan  (SCP) of the Republic of Bulgaria, and its amendments, the bodies and structures responsible for preparing and managing the implementation of the Plan, and their main functions.The Social Climate Plan of the Republic of Bulgaria is a national strategic document, developed in line with Regulation (EU) 2023/955 on the Social Climate Fund. Its purpose is to mitigate the social and economic impacts of the new Emissions Trading System (ETS2), which will cover the building sector and road transport.The draft of the SCP is currently open for public consultation.
Content of measure: The Social Climate Fund (SCF) was established under the 'Fit for 55' legislative package and represents a key instrument for mitigating the social consequences of the expansion of the European Union Emissions Trading System (ETS2). Its aim is to support vulnerable households, micro-enterprises, and transport users who will be affected by rising fuel and energy prices as a result of the green transition.In line with its commitments under Regulation (EU) 2023/955, Bulgaria is developing a Social Climate Plan (SCP) – a strategic document that includes a set of structural measures, temporary income support, and technical activities for the effective and inclusive implementation of ETS2 policies. The Plan is closely linked to the national climate and energy framework and complements the Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (INECP), the Long-term Strategy for the Renovation of the Building Stock, and the Territorial Just Transition Plans.Support for vulnerable households – through measures for energy efficiency, direct compensation for rising energy and transport costs, and targeted policies to eliminate energy poverty.Measures in the building sector – energy renovation of residential buildings, decarbonisation, replacement of heating technologies, and infrastructure development aimed at reducing carbon emissions and lowering heating costs.Measures in the transport sector – policies and investments in clean mobility, sustainable and public transport, and compensatory mechanisms to address the increase in fuel and transport service costs
Use of measure: n/a
Actors: National government; Social partners jointly; Other social actors (e.g. NGOs); Public employment service
Views of social partners: Civil and environmental NGOs (e.g. Za Zemiata, WWF, Greenpeace, Habitat Bulgaria):Generally support the idea of a Social Climate Plan but highlight weaknesses: lack of clarity on timeline and stages of preparation, very short deadlines, missing environmental assessment, and risk of inadequate coordination so close to the submission deadline.Employers’ organisations and trade unions (AOBE / BIA / BCCI / KRIB / AIKB together with CITUB and Podkrepa):In a joint statement ('Social Climate Plan – 4+2'), they insist that social partners must be active participants in the inter-ministerial working group and in the consultative council for implementation. They propose creating a 'Social Climate Observatory' to monitor energy poverty and oversee implementation, with the participation of both social partners and state institutions.NAMRB (National Association of Municipalities in Bulgaria):Notes that municipalities will play a key role in implementing SCP measures and announces that they will provide an official opinion on draft version 1.0 of the Plan.

Title: Grant scheme for supporting the resilience and adaptation to climate change of rural communities (2nd Call)
Title (national language): Σχέδιο χορηγιών για την ενίσχυση της ανθεκτικότητας και την προσαρμογή των κοινοτήτων στην κλιματική αλλαγ
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: The Grant Scheme aims to promote investments by rural councils in adaptation to climate change; particularly, it promotes adaptation to extreme temperatures, flooding and sustainable mobility whilst increasing the well-being of rural citizens. The Scheme is implemented under the 2nd Axis: ‘Accelerated Transition to a Green Economy’ of the Cyprus Recovery and Resilience Plan and the EU programme Next Generation EU and contributes to the achievement of the objectives of the National Adaptation Strategy and National Adaptation Action Plan, the Policy Statement for the Countryside and the Decision of the Council of Ministers No. 92.606/2021 for the Promotion of Integrated Policy Development and Support of Mountainous, Critical, Remote and other Target Areas.
Content of measure: Eligible to apply for the Scheme are local government authorities including community councils and partnerships or clusters of community councils operate in the areas covered by the Scheme. Municipalities or cluster of municipalities, natural persons performing economic activities, legal entities (i.e., businesses, associations), NGOs and legal entities governed by law are excluded from the grant.  The eligible actions and costs of the scheme include: * Consultant and expert fees (including designing and costing interventions, assistance in submitting applications, conducting and implementing public contracts, monitoring contract implementation, engineering services, architectural services etc)  * Tree planting in public pedestrian areas, community centers and squares, existing outdoor parking lots, public parks, green spaces, playgrounds, etc., with the aim of creating natural shade to help people cope with high temperatures and sun exposure. * Installation of urban equipment in public spaces, such as benches and fountains, with the aim of increasing visitor numbers and creating welcoming and comfortable spaces. * Construction of footpaths and/or modification and/or extension of existing footpaths in public transport areas.* Urban equipment along pedestrian paths, such as benches, bicycle stations, baskets, and fountains/drinking fountains.* Tree planting along existing and new (already registered) footpaths for natural shade.The percentage of funding is 100% of the actual eligible costs, excluding VAT. Each proposal must relate to investments with a minimum total estimated amount of €10,000, excluding VAT and the maximum grant amount is €50,000, excluding VAT.
Use of measure: The available budget of the Call is €500,000. The number of beneficiaries is currently unavailable as the implementation of the action is still runnin
Funding: European Funds; National funds; National Recovery and Resilience Facility
Views of social partners: No particular reactions from social partners have been recorded on the issue.

Title: Promoting energy efficiency & developing innovative approaches in schools
Title (national language): Προώθηση της ενεργειακής απόδοσης & ανάπτυξη καινοτόμων προσεγγίσεων στα σχολεί
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: The aim of the programme is to improve the energy efficiency and comfort conditions of public-school buildings in Cyprus contributing to the achievement of Cyprus National and European Energy and Climate Targets. The programme is funded through the Cohesion Policy Programme Thaleia 2021 – 2027, the European PDA programme (Project Development Assistance) and the Horizon 2020 programme ‘PEDIA’.
Content of measure: In May 2024 and after the pilot implementation of the energy upgrading of 5 school buildings, the Council of Ministers decided the continuation of the project with the energy upgrading of another 20 existing school buildings, of all levels of education. The implementation of the project is based on the model for assessing the energy upgrade needs of school building in Cyprus, which has been developed within the frame of the EU Horizon programme entitled ‘PEDIA’, aiming to convert these 25 school buildings into Nearly Zero Energy Buildings. The project is expected to facilitate the transition from fragmented, temporary, and isolated solutions to long-term holistic and permanent approaches, where the schools themselves, in addition to being zero-energy buildings, will become an integral part of the educational and social functions of the school.The interventions that are implemented for the upgrading of school buildings include the following actions, which comply with the requirements of the national legislation regarding the energy performance of buildings: - Installation of photovoltaic systems - Thermal insulation of roofs and walls- Replacement of windows- Replacement of lighting with LED lamps- Replacement of ventilation systems- Planting Within this frame, the implementation agency, the Cyprus Energy Agency, is launching an open tender for the energy upgrading of one school at a time, from the list of the selected schools that need energy upgrading.
Use of measure: The total budget of the programme is €20 million for the period March 2023 – December 2027. Up to September 2024, the energy upgrading of 5 schools have been completed and two new contracts have been signed for the upgrading of another 5 schools, with a budget of €2.3 million.
Views of social partners: No particular reactions from social partners have been recorded on the issue.

Title: Nearly Zero Energy Building Standard
Title (national language): Cladire cu consum de energie aproape zero
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: According to the provisions transposed into Romanian legislation, starting with  January 1 2019, all new buildings administered by public authorities are required to meet the minimum requirements of the Nearly zero energy building (NZEB) standard. Also, starting with 31 December 2022, Romanian national legislation imposes these minimum requirements on all newly constructed buildings.Although not mandatory, the NZEB standard can also be applied to existing buildings undergoing major renovations. On the other hand, according to the provisions of the law on the energy performance of buildings, in the case of major/extensive renovation, it is mandatory to improve energy performance in accordance with the requirements set out in the methodology MC001/2022 setting the maximum permissible values for primary energy consumption and CO2 emissions, considering technical, functional, and economic feasibility. Thus, as stipulated in the methodology, it is mandatory to cumulatively meet three minimum energy performance conditions, as is the case for new buildings, but in case of renovations  the maximum permissible limit values are lower, namely the minimum percentage provided by renewable sources is only 10%, if technically, economically, and environmentally feasible.European Directive 2010/31/EU on the energy performance of buildings (known as the EPBD – Energy Performance of Buildings Directive) sets minimum requirements for the energy performance of buildings and in Romania directives are transposed through specific laws and regulations. The authority that regulates aspects related to construction and energy efficiency of buildings is the ministry of development, public works, and administration (MDLPA).
Content of measure: One of the main direct benefits of NZEB buildings is the considerable reduction in energy costs, thanks to high energy efficiency and the use of renewable energy sources.In the long term, the savings generated are significant, and as energy prices rise, so will the savings generated. Moreover, improved energy efficiency also results in increased comfort and a healthier indoor environment. Indirectly, NZEB buildings contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, helping to combat climate change. Another indirect factor is the increase in property value due to energy-sustainable features.According to national expert organisation (e.g. Servelect), the biggest challenges in constructing a building to NZEB standards are the quality of execution and the correct implementation of the proposed solutions. The overall quality of work in these buildings is high, so the lack of specialized labour in this sector leads to various construction defects that are not consistent with the project's design data. Budget constraints represent another challenge. In the absence of a comprehensive initial budget, investment costs can rise unexpectedly quickly. As a result, beneficiaries tend to abandon solutions that may subsequently lead to higher operating costs.
Use of measure: No information about the use of the measure at this stage.
Views of social partners: There is no publicly available information about the social partners' views or reaction on the measure.

Occupations: Building and related trades workers, excluding electricians

Title: The Car Scrappage Plus programme
Title (national language): Rabla Plus 202
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: The programme consists of non-reimbursable financial grants, taking the form of eco-labels, from the Environment Fund, for the purchase of new motor vehicles by natural persons, in exchange for the scraping and deregistration of used motor vehicles. The purpose of the programme is to improve the quality of the environment through the purchase of new, less polluting and more energy-efficient motor vehicles. The programme aims to achieve the following environmental protection objectives of general interest:a) reducing the effects of air pollution and public health caused by exhaust emissions from used and energy-inefficient motor vehicles;b) preventing waste generation and achieving the objectives for recycling and recovery of waste from end-of-life vehicles.The multiannual program runs from 2025 to 2030 at national level.
Content of measure: Eligibility conditions that must be met by the applicant, a natural person, at the time of enrolment in the program:a) has their domicile/residence in Romania, b) has fulfilled their obligations to pay taxes, fines, and contributions to the state budget and local budget where they are domiciled/resident, in accordance with the legal provisions in force,c) has not been convicted of environmental crimes by a final court decision,d) undertakes to hand over to an authorized collector a used motor vehicle owned by him or the transferor, e) undertakes to deregister the used motor vehicle from the traffic register.The applicant may obtain one or more eco-labels during a registration session in exchange for handing over an equivalent number of used vehicles for scrapping. Multiple eco-labels cannot be accumulated for the purchase of a new motor vehicle. The amount of the eco-label is:•	10,000 RON (approx. €2,000) for the purchase of a new vehicle with a thermal propulsion system or a motorcycle,•	12,000 RON (approx. €2,400) for the purchase of a new vehicle with a hybrid propulsion system,•	15,000 RON (approx. €3,000) for the purchase of a new hybrid plug-in motor vehicle or an electric motorcycle,•	 37,000 RON (approx. €7,400) for the purchase of a new pure electric motor vehicle or a motor vehicle with a hydrogen fuel cell,•	120,000 RON (approx. €24,000) for the purchase of a new plug-in hybrid or pure electric vehicle for public institutions and administrative-territorial units.
Use of measure: The total budget of the programme is 610 million RON (approx. €122 million). No information about the amount spent at this stage.
Views of social partners: There is no publicly available information about the social partners' views or reaction on the measure.
Sectors: C29 Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers

Title: Subsidy scheme for solar panels for the production of hot water
Title (national language): Σχέδιο χορηγιών για ηλιακά συστήματα παραγωγής ζεστού νερού σε κατοικίες
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: The Scheme aims to provide financial incentives, in the form of non-repayable grants, for the installation or replacement of solar hot water systems in existing homes. It is implemented in accordance with the provisions of Article 5 of the ‘Renewable Energy Sources and Energy Saving Fund Operation Law’ of 2022 (Law 108(I)/2022) and funded by the Renewable Energy Sources and Energy Conservation Fund of the Republic of Cyprus.
Content of measure: Beneficiaries to apply for the subsidy scheme are natural persons that intent to invest in the installation or replacement of an integrated solar hot water heating system – i.e., hot water cylinder and solar panels – in an existing home. The applicant is not required to be the owner of the house as soon as the invoices related to the investment are issued in his/her name. Legal persons are excluded from the subsidy. The properties in which the investment will be made must be a residence. The application for the building permit and/or urban planning permit for the residence must be have submitted before the 31/12/2011. Residences that are rented by legal entities and residences used for economic activities are excluded from the subsidy.    Eligible are only the solar system installation that are installed by the installers included in the list of participants of the scheme. Additionally, the equipment to be installed (cylinder and panels) must be included in the list of the eligible equipment as defined by the scheme.  The amount of subsidy is €500 per residence, which increased to €900 for both residences in the mountainous areas and for residences of the vulnerable electricity consumers, as defined by the Decrees 308/2023 and 309/2023 for the definition of energy poverty and vulnerable consumers, respectively.
Use of measure: The budget of the Scheme is €1 million and it is expected that 2,000 applications will be subsidized.
Views of social partners: No particular reactions have been recorded.

Title: National mobility bonus for sustainable transport purchase
Title (national language): Bonus mobilità nazionale per l'acquisto di mezzi di trasporto sostenibili
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: The mobility bonus was introduced through the Decreto Rilancio (Legislative Decree No. 34/2020) as part of Italy's response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The measure aimed to promote sustainable mobility alternatives during a period when public transport capacity was significantly reduced due to health restrictions. The initiative was implemented through the Decreto 14 agosto 2020 establishing the Programma sperimentale buono mobilità (Experimental Mobility Bonus Program). The policy sought to encourage environmentally friendly transport solutions whilst supporting economic recovery in the bicycle and micromobility sectors. The program was specifically designed for residents of larger urban areas where alternative transport options were most viable and where air quality improvements could have the greatest impact.
Content of measure: The program provided a 60% subsidy, capped at €500, for purchasing bicycles (including electric-assisted models), electric scooters, hoverboards, segways and other sustainable mobility devices. Eligibility was restricted to adult residents of regional capitals, metropolitan cities, provincial capitals, and municipalities with populations exceeding 50,000 inhabitants. The initiative operated through two phases: Phase 1 covered purchases made between 4 May and 2 November 2020, offering post-purchase reimbursements; Phase 2 covered purchases from 3 November to 31 December 2020, providing direct discounts at participating retailers. Applications were processed through the dedicated platform www.buonomobilita.it, requiring SPID (Sistema Pubblico di Identità Digitale) authentication. The total program budget allocated €215 million for subsidising sustainable transport purchases. A click day system was implemented on 3 November for processing reimbursement applications, followed by a pre-registration period for excluded applicants
Use of measure: The program successfully funded 558,725 purchases, utilising the full €215 million budget. Of the 590,188 users who registered on the platform, 257,949 received vouchers for future purchases whilst 300,776 obtained reimbursements for previous acquisitions. The beneficiary profile showed a male majority (63% of purchases) with 86.6% aged between 26-65 years. Bicycles accounted for 73% of subsidised purchases (483,474 units), whilst electric micromobility devices represented 25% (165,573 units). A subsequent pre-registration phase recorded 206,083 additional users requesting approximately €35.6 million in reimbursements for excluded applicants. The program demonstrated significant public interest in sustainable mobility solutions, though digital divide issues affected access for some potential beneficiaries during the technical difficulties experienced on the click day
Views of social partners: No involvement

Title: Ecobonus for sustainable mobility
Title (national language): Ecobonus per la mobilità sostenibile
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: The Ecobonus automotive scheme was established through Law No. 178/2020 (Budget Law 2021) as part of Italy's commitment to reducing CO2 emissions and renewing the national vehicle fleet. The measure aligns with environmental objectives outlined in the PNIEC (Piano Nazionale Integrato per l'Energia e il Clima) and the 2030 Agenda, following European air quality regulations. The programme received significant updates through Ministerial Decree 20 May 2024, which introduced enhanced support for low-income households and expanded coverage to include used vehicles and retrofitting options. The initiative is managed by Invitalia, Italy's national development agency, and operates through a network of authorised dealers who apply discounts directly at purchase. The scheme addresses both environmental goals and industrial policy objectives by supporting the transition to cleaner mobility whilst sustaining the automotive sector.
Content of measure: The Ecobonus provides purchase incentives for low-emission vehicles across multiple categories: M1 (passenger cars), L1e-L7e (motorcycles and mopeds), and N1-N2 (commercial vehicles). For 2025, individual buyers with family income up to €30,000 receive €11,000 for electric vehicle purchases with mandatory scrapping of Euro 0-5 vehicles, whilst those with family income between €30,001-€40,000 receive €9,000 under the same conditions. Microenterprises can access up to 30% of purchase price (maximum €20,000) for electric commercial vehicles. Eligibility requires residence in municipalities exceeding 50,000 inhabitants, purchase of 100% electric vehicles with list price up to €35,000 (excluding VAT), and ownership of scrapped vehicles for at least 12 months. Additional incentives cover motorcycle purchases (30% without scrapping, 40% with scrapping) and retrofitting existing vehicles with GPL or methane systems. The total programme budget allocates €150 million: €20 million annually from 2021-2023 and €30 million annually for 2024-2026.
Use of measure: Based on data updated on 19 September 2025, the Ecobonus programme shows significant uptake with 14,128 vehicle reservations recorded nationally. Data reveals substantial regional variation in programme utilisation, with northern regions demonstrating higher participation rates. Vehicle category breakdown indicates strong demand across different segments: L4 motorcycles account for the largest share with 5,459 reservations, followed by L3 motorcycles with 4,326 units. L7 vehicles recorded 2,230 reservations, whilst L1 category shows 1,707 bookings. Smaller categories include L2 with 359 reservations and L5 with 47 units.
Views of social partners: UNRAE (the union of foreign brand vehicle dealers) expressed being caught off guard by the unannounced incentive programme, criticising the lack of stakeholder consultation. Director General warned that announcing incentives without complete implementation details risks paralysing market demand, stating that incentives should arrive as concrete decisions rather than promises requiring clarification.The association raised concerns about numerous eligibility restrictions: mandatory scrapping, family income thresholds, and urban residence requirements. Despite these procedural criticisms, UNRAE acknowledged the programme's potential as Italy's largest-ever annual electric vehicle incentive scheme.

Title: Jedlik district heating support for service providers
Title (national language): Jedlik Ányos távhõ támogatás beruházóknak
Category: Promoting the economic, labour market and social recovery into a green future
Background information: District heating systems provide heating to more than 1.5 million people in some 700,000 households throughout Hungary. As of 2025, 210 district heating systems were in operation in the country. The programme, launched as part of the Ányos Jedlik Energy Programme, is aimed to be the largest programme supporting district heating service providers over the past 35 years. The first phase of the programme was published by the National Energy Agency NEÜ under call number 2025/MA/TÁVHŐ/01.
Content of measure: The total budget of the programme’s first phase is HUF 45 billion. One applicant can request a subsidy of minimum HUF 20m and maximum HUF 1.5bn (€50,490-3.8m).The following types of projects can be subsidised to the full amount:a) Separation of service provider heating centers, modernization of user heating centers. b) Replacement of primary district heating pipes (including operational and structural elements forming part of the heating infrastructure), and thermal insulation and underground installation of above-ground district heating pipes (using pre-insulated pipes laid directly in the ground).c) Construction of heat storage facilities and connection to the district heating system.d) Development of district heating systems to create and improve energy supply options based on renewable and/or residual heat from renewable sources, up to the heat transfer limit, but no further than the boundary of the heat production site.
Use of measure: There is no information about uptake as yet.
Actors: National government; Company / Companies; EU (Council, EC, EP)
Views of social partners: The  Association of Hungarian District Heating Providers ( _Magyar Távhőszolgáltatók Szakmai Szövetsége_ ) suggested that the maximum amount of the grant should be raised to HUF 2.5bn. (€6.3m).
Sectors: D35 Electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply
